title: Productive, Vendor-Neutral GPU Programming Using Chapel
problem: The HPC programming ecosystem requires learning multiple GPU frameworks (CUDA, HIP, SYCL, OpenACC, Kokkos) alongside traditional parallelism models (MPI, OpenMP), making GPU programming for clusters and supercomputers unnecessarily complex.
motivation: GPUs are increasingly prevalent in HPC and AI, so reducing programming complexity and improving developer productivity is critical for broader HPC adoption.
method: Chapel is a programming language that treats parallelism (splitting work across processors) and locality (where data sits in memory) as concepts you directly express in your code. Instead of writing separate code for different GPU frameworks, you write once in Chapel, and the compiler translates it to CUDA, HIP, or whatever framework you're using. This avoids the tedious and error-prone work of managing multiple GPU programming models.
key_novelty: A programming language that lets you write GPU code once and automatically translates it to work with any vendor's GPU framework (CUDA, HIP, etc.).
contributions: Chapel GPU programming support with vendor-neutral abstractions for GPU parallelism
Demonstration that Chapel's language features significantly simplify GPU programming compared to traditional frameworks
Successful porting of coral reef biodiversity image analysis application to GPU
Initial performance evaluation on Frontier supercomputer
primary_theme: Vendor-neutral GPU programming through language abstractions
